title: A Echo for the Protocol
premise: Marguerite Dravenmoor smuggles memories between the two fleets that split humanity's colonies a generation ago, keeping his head down and his cargo deniable. When the derelict ship Vesperine docks at Meridian Station with its crew aged backward into children who remember a future that hasn't happened, both fleets claim it as proof of the other's secret weapons program. Marguerite discovers the Vesperine's captain was his lost lover, Sefa, now a child carrying an intact memory-core of their shared future—and the truce holding the fleets apart expires in thirty days. To keep the peace, Marguerite must smuggle one last, impossible memory: a fabricated record proving the Vesperine's anomaly was natural, sacrificing his own history with Sefa to seed the lie. In the end he burns his smuggling network, gives the child-Sefa her future back unopened, and chooses exile on the station—belonging, at last, to no fleet and to everyone.
about_author: Dominic Brightwater is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years coordinating freight between rival colonial blocs before turning to fiction. He writes from a houseboat on the Tagus, where he claims the river traffic taught him everything he knows about smuggling and patience.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Marguerite runs contraband memories through customs at Meridian Station, narrating his methods and his rule: never carry anything you can't deny. A routine bribe goes wrong when customs officer Ilsa Vane lets him pass too easily—he suspects she knows something. POV: Marguerite. Beat: wary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Dock
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present-day docking fees: how the Concord and the Verity fleets split after the Sundering War, and why memory-smuggling became treason in both. Marguerite delivers a widow's recorded wedding day across the line. POV: Marguerite. Beat: tenderness inside criminality; establish stakes of the divided worlds.

chapters.title: Something Wrong With the Light
chapters.summary: A ship appears at the system edge on a trajectory no living pilot could have flown. Station sensors read its hull as decades older than its registry. Marguerite, docked nearby, watches the panic begin through his cargo-cam network. POV: Marguerite, with interludes from Ilsa Vane's logs. Beat: dread arriving quietly.

chapters.title: Vesperine
chapters.summary: The derelict docks itself. Rescue teams find forty-one crew aged backward into children under ten, physically healthy, remembering nothing—or claiming nothing. One girl, maybe seven, looks at Marguerite through the quarantine glass and says his name. POV: Marguerite. Beat: shock; the past reaching for him.

chapters.title: Quarantine Rules
chapters.summary: Both fleets demand custody of the Vesperine children. Station administrator Okonkwo stalls, citing neutral-port law. Marguerite learns the girl is Sefa Ilves—his lover, lost twelve years ago on a deep-range survey—now a child with sealed memories. POV: Marguerite. Beat: grief colliding with duty.

chapters.title: What the Girl Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa-child dreams aloud in fragments: a treaty signing, a fire, Marguerite older. Fleet intelligence officers circle the quarantine ward like sharks. Marguerite realizes her mind holds a memory-core recording of events that haven't happened—including the war both fleets are sliding toward. POV: Marguerite. Beat: terrible hope.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Price
chapters.summary: Customs officer Ilsa Vane reveals she's Concord intelligence and has known Marguerite's routes for years. She offers immunity for him and protection for Sefa if he helps extract the memory-core before the Verity fleet does. POV: Ilsa, primarily. Beat: seduction of the lawful option; moral compromise begins.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: News breaks: the armistice expires in thirty days, and both fleets are mobilizing over the Vesperine 'weapon.' Marguerite maps the factions—Concord hardliners, Verity hawks, Okonkwo's fragile neutrality. POV: ensemble via station broadcast fragments. Beat: rising pressure; the world narrows toward war.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Marguerite visits the ward legally, reading to Sefa. She recites details of their life together she couldn't know—the boat on Callisto, the argument about names. He understands the core isn't prophecy; it's a recording of a future someone lived and sent back. POV: Marguerite. Beat: love rekindled in impossible form; heartbreak sharpening.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marguerite weighs options with his fence, Doss: steal the core for Concord, sell it to Verity, destroy it, or forge something new. Destroying it might erase Sefa's only chance to be whole again. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the central dilemma crystallized—her future versus everyone's present.

chapters.title: Verity Comes Calling
chapters.summary: A Verity agent, Commander Ash Rell, corners Marguerite with proof of his smuggling and a counteroffer: help Verity take the children, and they'll reveal what really happened to the original Vesperine voyage—a survey Marguerite funded. POV: Rell, then Marguerite. Beat: the trap closes from both sides.

chapters.title: The Original Voyage
chapters.summary: Rell's files show the Vesperine found a temporal fold near a dead star—an accident, not a weapon—and tried to send a warning back. The message never arrived because someone in the Concord chain of command buried it. POV: flashback documents, Marguerite's frame. Beat: revelation; the enemy is bureaucracy, not the other fleet.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Gambit
chapters.summary: Administrator Okonkwo privately asks Marguerite—the man nobody suspects—to do what diplomats can't: get the truth out without either fleet losing face. He needs a story both sides can believe. POV: Okonkwo. Beat: reluctant alliance; the smuggler becomes the messenger.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Marguerite, Ilsa, and Doss run a three-way con to move Sefa and four other eldest children out of the ward before Concord seizes them. It half-works: Sefa is safe in Marguerite's quarters, but Doss is captured, and Ilsa's cover is burned. POV: Marguerite. Beat: action peak of the middle act; cost made real.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Doss
chapters.summary: Doss holds out for two days, then gives up Marguerite's route codes—not out of betrayal, but because Concord promises the children medical care. Marguerite must decide whether to hate him. POV: Doss. Beat: loyalty strained by love; no clean villains.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Okonkwo craft the forgery: a complete, convincing memory-record showing the Vesperine anomaly as a natural temporal fold, witnessed neutrally, threatening no one. To make it credible, it must be seeded from inside Sefa's own core—which means editing her, risking the self she might become. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the moral crux; justice outside the law demands a sin.

chapters.title: Sefa's Choice
chapters.summary: Child-Sefa, sharp beyond her years, works out what he's planning. She offers her consent: 'If I'm her, she'd want the worlds to keep talking.' But she asks one thing—that he open the true core afterward and remember her properly. POV: Sefa. Beat: devastating grace; love against duty resolved by the smallest voice.

chapters.title: Truce Day
chapters.summary: The forged record surfaces simultaneously in both fleets' channels, corroborated by Okonkwo's staged 'neutral audit.' Hardliners scramble; mobilization pauses. Concord tries to arrest Marguerite; Ilsa burns her career covering his escape. POV: multiple, rapid cuts. Beat: climax—the lie takes hold as the clock hits zero.

chapters.title: What the Core Held
chapters.summary: Alone, Marguerite opens the true memory-core. He lives the future Sefa recorded: their reunion, the war averted differently, her death old and unafraid. The core also holds the Vesperine crew's final message, which he transmits openly—truth after the lie has done its work. POV: Marguerite. Beat: catharsis; grief and gratitude entwined.

chapters.title: The Fleets Blink
chapters.summary: With the final message public, both fleets stand down rather than fight over an accident neither caused. Negotiations resume at Meridian. Ilsa, disgraced but free, chooses to stay; Rell withdraws with a nod that almost resembles respect. POV: ensemble. Beat: resolution of the political arc; exhausted relief.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Sefa, her edited memories stable, begins growing up on the station among the other returned children. She doesn't remember Marguerite as her lover—but she remembers him as home. He signs on as the station's licensed courier, running honest cargo between reconciling worlds. POV: Marguerite. Beat: quiet joy; belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: An Echo for the Protocol
chapters.summary: Years later, an adult Sefa joins the first joint fleet expedition back to the temporal fold. Before launch she gives Marguerite a recording—one memory, freely given, of the woman she might have been to him. He plays it once, then adds it to the station's public archive so no one ever owns the future alone again. POV: Marguerite. Beat: bittersweet closure; the echo outlasts the protocol.
